title: Post-POC Readout — Quantify & Decision Paths
content:
Executive summary:

This document summarizes the 6-week ACME POC (Jan 6–Feb 14, 2026) for an LLM-powered customer support summarization pipeline, captures the quantitative outcomes vs. success criteria, and lays out recommended deployment and next-step actions. The POC proved the inference approach is viable for ACME's SLA targets and regulatory constraints, with three recommended deployment paths depending on procurement timeframe and security requirements.

POC objectives (as scoped):
- Validate model quality for multi-channel customer support summaries (email + chat) with F1/ROUGE-style metrics and curated prompts.
- Demonstrate 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for 512-token context under 50 concurrent users representative load.
- Show steady-state per-token cost guidance and expected annualized cost for 1M requests/month.
- Exercise Private deployment networking and KMS integration to confirm compliance needs.

Success criteria (agreed with ACME):
- Quality: Human-rated summary accept/reject >= 88% on 200-case blind eval.
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms for single-request path in production-like load.
- Reliability: <1% error rate during 72-hour stress run.
- Integrations: VPC peering + KMS key rotation demonstrated in staging.

Outcomes and measured results:
- Quality: Blind eval (n=250) mean accept rate = 91% (stdev 4.1%). Notable failure modes: long-thread context truncation in 7% of rejects; hallucination on unstructured logs 3%.
- Latency: Observed p50/p95 = 120ms / 310ms when using Redwood-hosted model variant rwlm-v2-small-q4 under batching policy (max_batch=8, max_latency_ms=15). Without batching, p95 rose to ~680ms.
- Throughput: Sustained 50 concurrent users mapped to ~420 RPS at steady-state with batching and caching; average tokens/request = 420.
- Reliability: 0.6% transient errors during a single 6-hour GPU maintenance test (automatic fallback to rwlm-v2-medium occurred as configured).
- Cost: Modeled per-token cost (hosted routing + caching) = $0.00065/token; projected monthly spend for 1M requests = ~$58k (assumes average 420 tokens/request). Dedicated capacity pricing estimate reduces unit cost by ~38% at 2k reserved RPS equivalent.
- Security: VPC peering completed in staging; KMS integration demonstrated with rotation cadence 90 days. No plaintext logs left in customer-visible S3 buckets; audit trail captured.

Key learnings and technical notes:
- Batching and prefix KV caching were the largest unit-cost levers — enabling batching policies improved effective throughput and reduced p95 by ~55% vs no batching.
- Model variant selection: rwlm-v2-small-q4 satisfies latencies and cost for most tickets. Higher fidelity cases (legal/regulatory) require rwlm-v2-medium (no-quant) or an on-call fallback to hosted rwlm-v2-large for long contexts.
- Context handling: For very long email threads we recommend server-side stitching + selective summarization prompts to avoid truncation-induced hallucinations.
- Autoscaling: Short cooldowns (30s) with progressive warm-up helped maintain p95 during bursts; cold-start penalty persists for new model containers (measured ~220ms).
- Observability: Token-level traces and per-route SLO dashboards were critical in debugging a prompt-induced output divergence during week 3.

Recommended deployment options (tradeoff summary):
1) Hosted Redwood API (fastest time-to-value):
   - Pros: Quick rollout (2–3 weeks), lowest procurement friction, built-in autoscaling and fallbacks.
   - Cons: Data residency constraints for regulated tickets; lesser control over reserved capacity.
   - When to pick: ACME pilot with non-sensitive traffic and fast ROI needs.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
   - Pros: Predictable latency and unit costs; private capacity pools with SLA commitments.
   - Cons: Requires capacity commit (30–60 days procurement), integration work for autoscaling policies.
   - When to pick: If ACME expects >=2k sustained RPS in 6–12 months or wants consistent unit economics.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem):
   - Pros: Full network control, compliance with strict PII/regulatory rules, KMS/HSM integration.
   - Cons: Longest lead time (8–12 weeks), heavier ops on customer side, potential higher TCO unless amortized by large volume.
   - When to pick: Sensitive workflows and legal/regulatory cases (customer noted financial litigation use-cases).

Recommended immediate next steps (concrete owners & dates):
- Decision call with ACME execs to pick deployment path (owner: Maya Chen, target: 2026-03-20).
- If Hosted selected: pilot rollout to 5% traffic using rwlm-v2-small-q4 + prefix caching + canary route (owner: Jordan Lee, target: 2026-04-02).
- If Dedicated selected: procurement kickoff + capacity proposal acceptance (owner: Samir Patel, target: 2026-03-30). Engineering prework: capacity reservation blueprint + autoscaler policy (owner: Diego Ramos, due: 2026-04-09).
- If Private selected: schedule on-site network workshop and HSM/KMS KTR runbook signoff (owner: Eleanor Brooks + ACME network lead, target: 2026-04-20).
- Quality gating: prepare 1,000-case blind eval harness and acceptance checklist (owner: Customer Success — Nina Alvarez & Jordan Lee, due: 2026-04-14).

Risks, mitigations, and open questions:
- Risk: Procurement timeline pushes to Dedicated/Private causing pilot stall. Mitigation: Dual-track plan — start hosted pilot for <10% non-sensitive traffic while procurement progresses for Dedicated/Private.
- Risk: Long-thread hallucinations for certain ticket types. Mitigation: Implement thread-trimming heuristics and targeted evaluator tests; route flagged tickets to higher-fidelity model.
- Open question: ACME compliance team requests on-prem deployment for some customers only — need scoping for hybrid routing (partial Private connectivity). Action: Architecture scoping session on 2026-03-22.
- Operational risk: On-call team readiness for model rollouts. Mitigation: Runbook, canary windows, and simulated failover tested during POC; recommend 2-week post-launch hypercare.

Cost appendix (top-level estimates):
- Hosted: ~$58k/mo (1M req/mo, avg 420 tokens/request, current hosted pricing with caching).
- Dedicated: ~38% lower unit cost at 2k reserved RPS depending on commit term (proposal to be finalized by Samir).
- Private: Higher up-front setup (estimated engineering effort 6–10 person-weeks) and infra cost; amortized unit cost similar to Dedicated at high volumes.

Stakeholder workshop notes (selected):
- ACME PM Nina: prioritized latency and auditability; willing to accept small increase in monthly ops cost for gold-standard audit trails.
- ACME Legal: requires KMS + key rotation audit; asked for proof of “no plaintext export” in logs (we demonstrated staging setup).
- ACME Infra: prefers VPC peering with dedicated NAT gateways; asked for runbook for failover to other region.
- Redwood SRE: recommended canary + automatic fallback routing to rwlm-v2-medium when error rate >1.5%.

Acceptance criteria for go/no-go pilot (must be green to go to production):
- Production-like 72-hour run shows p95 <= 350ms and error rate <1%.
- Blind eval accept rate >= 88% on 1,000 sampling.
- VPC & KMS integration validated in staging and SOC log review complete.

Appendix (artifacts produced during POC):
- Evaluation harness: /artifacts/acme/poc/eval-harness-v3 (scorecards and prompts)
- Load test reports: load-report-2026-02-09.csv (RPS/latency traces)
- Observability dashboards: route-slo-summary (shared link in Confluence)

Final recommendation (short):
Start a dual-track approach: 1) kickoff a hosted pilot for non-sensitive traffic immediately to capture early wins and metrics, and 2) parallel procurement scoping for Dedicated capacity with a target commit if volume forecasts hold. If ACME legal requires, plan Private deployment for specific regulated customers and scope hybrid routing.

Notes to follow-up in the decision call:
- Confirm procurement timeline and sign-off owner at ACME (Nina).
- Confirm whether 10% of traffic can be used for hosted pilot.
- Agree on canary windows and hypercare staffing.

Prepared by: Maya Chen (Solutions Engineering)
Document history: Drafted 2026-02-18; updated with week-6 load tests 2026-03-12.
